description: The first checkpoint, done by an IDO Officer or the IDO Chairperson. Four mutually exclusive outcomes: recommend it onward, return it to the requestor to fix, reject it outright, or defer it to next year's PPMP. Recommending is also where the final title, the reference and the processor are set.

hooks.note: Reads request.getById; a thin wrapper so the page does not import the requestor's hook.
The four actions plus isAnyPending, so one in-flight action disables the other three.

functional: The four actions are mutually exclusive and each is terminal for this stage — there is no undo.
Recommend requires a final title. It is the title that appears on the PDF and in every later screen, so it cannot be left blank.
finalTitle REPLACES the requestor's title in the UI: the detail page shows finalTitle with the original beneath it. title itself is never overwritten (this resolves the IRMS-old open question).
processor is stamped with the reviewer's name at recommendation time and is what the requestor's side rail shows.
requestStartAt is set on the first recommendation only; a second write would lose when the work actually started.

The budget stage is conditional: directorReviewStatus becomes UNDER_BUDGET_OFFICER_REVIEW only when at least one BUDGET_OFFICER account exists. With none, the request goes straight to UNDER_DIRECTOR_REVIEW.
masterStatus becomes UNDER_DIRECTOR_REVIEW on recommend regardless of the budget branch — the requestor's view does not expose the internal split.
Notes on return and reject are required; the note on defer is optional.
When the request has moved past this stage the page still opens, read-only, showing what was decided and by whom. No control is rendered that would throw.
authorization: Server gate: every one of the four procedures is a roleProcedure over the same two roles, then assertPermission(REVIEW_REQUEST), then the status check.
The status check (SUBMITTED or UNDER_IDO_REVIEW) is what stops a second IDO officer acting on a request that has already moved on.
A DIRECTOR or BUDGET_OFFICER calling any of these gets FORBIDDEN from roleProcedure even though they are staff.
The requestor cannot call any of them, and cannot edit the request once it leaves DRAFT or RETURNED (spec 005).
ux: The page reads like the request, not like a form: same layout as create/edit, read-only, so a reviewer is looking at what the requestor filled in (an explicit IRMS-old fix).
Destructive actions are grouped and visually secondary to Recommend; Reject and Defer are terminal and must not sit under the thumb.
Each destructive action asks for its note in a modal before it fires — never a bare confirm.
While any action is pending all four controls are disabled, so a slow network cannot produce two outcomes.
When the request is not actionable the panel explains why in a sentence naming the current stage, rather than hiding silently.

acceptance_criteria.then: masterStatus is UNDER_DIRECTOR_REVIEW, directorReviewStatus is UNDER_BUDGET_OFFICER_REVIEW, and it appears in the budget officer's queue

acceptance_criteria.given: a SUBMITTED request and no BUDGET_OFFICER account at all
acceptance_criteria.then: directorReviewStatus is UNDER_DIRECTOR_REVIEW and it appears in the director's queue

acceptance_criteria.then: the modal shows 'Note is required' and no call is made

edge_cases: The budget-officer count is read at recommendation time. Creating a budget officer afterwards does not retro-route requests already sent to the director, and that is correct — do not add a migration that rewrites them.
requestStartAt must be written only when null, or a re-recommendation (which the status guard should prevent anyway) would move the start date.
Recommend writes six columns plus an audit log; all of it belongs in one transaction, or a failure halfway leaves a request with a final title and no status change.
The status guard reads masterStatus, but the budget and director stages read their own columns. Mixing the two is how a request becomes actionable at two desks at once.

approverNote is a single column reused by later stages in the PDF; a later note overwrites the IDO's. That is the existing behaviour and the PDF prints it in both the Reason and Notes blocks — do not treat the duplication as a bug without deciding what the printed form should say.
Defer and reject look similar and are both terminal, but they mean opposite things to a requestor. The copy on each control must say which is which.
out_of_scope: The IDO Chairperson's FINAL review — spec 013; a plain officer can never do that one.
Re-opening a rejected or deferred request — there is no such action; the requestor files a new one.
Assigning a specific officer — processor is stamped, not assigned.
